user_text: Summarize the benefits of code review for a small team.
assistant_text:
# Benefits of Code Review for a Small Team

## Quality & Reliability
- **Catches bugs early** before they reach production
- **Enforces consistency** in coding style and standards
- **Reduces technical debt** by encouraging cleaner solutions

## Knowledge Sharing
- **Spreads expertise** so no single person owns all the knowledge
- **Onboards new members faster** through exposure to the codebase
- **Documents decisions** within the review discussion itself

## Team Collaboration
- **Builds shared ownership** — everyone feels responsible for the code
- **Encourages communication** and constructive feedback habits
- **Reduces bus factor** (risk of losing critical knowledge if someone leaves)

## Risk Reduction
- **Second set of eyes** catches logic errors the author may overlook
- **Validates requirements** are actually met before merging
- **Prevents security vulnerabilities** from slipping through

## Practical Tips for Small Teams
- Keep reviews **short and focused** (under 400 lines at a time)
- Set a **time limit** (e.g., review within 24 hours) to avoid bottlenecks
- Use it as a **learning opportunity**, not a gatekeeping exercise

---

**Bottom line:** Even with limited people, code review pays off by improving quality, spreading knowledge, and reducing costly mistakes down the line.
Code review helps small teams catch bugs early, share knowledge, and maintain higher code quality through collaborative feedback.

1. **Bug detection** – A second reviewer catches errors the original author overlooked before they reach production.
2. **Knowledge sharing** – Team members learn the codebase and spread expertise, reducing reliance on any single person.
Code review builds a sense of **shared ownership**, encouraging everyone on the team to feel collectively responsible for the quality of the codebase.

user_text: State one risk if reviews are skipped.
assistant_text: If code reviews are skipped, bugs and security vulnerabilities are more likely to slip into production, potentially causing costly outages or data breaches.
Track **defect escape rate** — the number of bugs found in production versus those caught during review — to measure how effectively your review process is preventing issues from reaching users.
Code review is a small investment that pays dividends in quality, collaboration, and long-term team health.

• Code review catches bugs early and improves overall code quality.
• It promotes knowledge sharing and reduces reliance on any single team member.
• It builds a culture of shared ownership and accountability.
• Skipping reviews risks costly bugs and security vulnerabilities in production.
• Track defect escape rate to measure review effectiveness.
• The small time investment pays off in long-term team health and reliability.
Code review is a simple practice that keeps code clean, teams aligned, and production stable.
Code review is only effective if feedback is constructive and timely — poorly managed reviews can slow development and damage team morale.
Bad reviews hurt teams; keep feedback kind, fast, and focused.
Code review boosts quality and collaboration, but only works well when feedback is timely, constructive, and focused.
